outcome: Persistent subclinical myocardial dysfunction (defined as left ventricular global longitudinal strain less negative than -20% in postpartum)
cohort: The study included 46 pregnant women with obesity and 83 age-, ethnicity-, and gestational week-matched pregnant women without obesity.
finding: Pregnant women with obesity exhibited significantly lower myocardial strain indices and a higher risk of persistent subclinical myocardial dysfunction over the postpartum period compared to women without obesity.
